answer: Judgment: FY26 targeted productivity (>$500m) looks mainly like an offset to continuing wage, banker and UNITE investment pressure, not a mechanism sufficient on its own to restore positive jaws. Neither document uses the word 'jaws,' gives FY26 revenue/income growth guidance, or states a CTI target, so no disclosed jaws forecast exists; this judgment is inferred from the expense side only. In FY25, the Group expense bridge ran FY24 $10,944m -> Staff costs +$397m -> Technology +$146m -> Volume and other +$199m -> Productivity ($402m) -> Investments +$359m (UNITE investment $399m, amortisation +$106m, partly offset by lower ex-UNITE spend) -> Restructuring charge +$273m -> FY25 $11,916m (+9%, +6% ex restructuring). Net operating income grew only 3%, so FY25 jaws compute to roughly -6ppts (-3ppts ex restructuring), and the results announcement states outright that 'Productivity provided a partial offset' -- not a full one. On investment mix, FY25 investment spend was $1,918m (+9%): UNITE $660m (34%, a large increase from $147m), Growth & productivity $563m (30%), Risk & regulatory $695m (36%, -34%). UNITE's FY25 expensed share is disclosed as 74% in the results announcement versus 76% in the presentation -- an unreconciled discrepancy; the announcement is preferred as the primary lodged disclosure. FY26 UNITE spend is guided to $850-950m at ~75% expensed, implying an expensed UNITE cost of roughly $638-712m versus FY25's actual ~$488-502m -- a step-up of about $135-225m, which alone is equal to a third to nearly half of the entire FY26 productivity target. Layering on FY26 EBA increases of 3-4% against a $6,326m FY25 staff base and continued 'investment in bankers,' the identified cost pressures plausibly approach or exceed the incremental productivity gain (the >$500m FY26 target is only about $100m above FY25's realised $402m). UNITE's disclosed duration/expensing profile: the program extends into FY29; cumulative spend to Sep-25 was $807m, ~40% of total planned FY25-1H29 investment (implying a total program cost near $2.0bn, though never stated directly); FY27-28 UNITE spend is guided at ~40% of a ~$2bn p.a. Group investment envelope; FY29 spend is guided lower; and the average capitalised-software amortisation period shortened to 2.7 years from 3.1 years, meaning capitalised UNITE spend will hit the P&L faster than before.

limitations: Neither document uses the term 'jaws,' and neither gives FY26 revenue, income, or NIM growth guidance or a CTI target, so a disclosed FY26 jaws forecast does not exist; the judgment here is inferred from expense-side arithmetic only, not confirmed by WBC.
UNITE's FY25 expensed proportion is inconsistent between the two source documents (74% in the results announcement vs 76% in the presentation), and this was not reconciled.
The implied ~$2.0bn total UNITE program cost is derived by dividing $807m by ~40%; WBC does not state a single total program cost figure anywhere in either document.
Whether the $273m FY25 Fit for Growth restructuring charge recurs, in whole or part, in FY26 is not disclosed.

The composition of the >$500m FY26 productivity target (how much comes from Fit for Growth restructuring vs. UNITE initiative-level benefits, which sum to only about $165m across the four initiatives with disclosed dollar benefits) is not itemised.

The EBA-increase and banker-investment dollar impact on FY26 staff costs is not quantified by WBC beyond the 3-4% EBA rate and qualitative 'investment in bankers' language; any dollar comparison against the productivity target uses the disclosed FY25 staff cost base as an illustrative scale, not a WBC-provided FY26 figure.
